source_refs.note: Scalar or Dot Product: a main subheading of 2.3 Product of two vectors, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 25-25.

blocks.text: The scalar product of two vectors A⃗ and B⃗ is written as A⃗.B⃗ and is defined as
where A and B are the magnitudes of vectors A⃗ and B⃗ and θ is the angle between them.

blocks.alt: Two parts. (a) Vector A along the base and vector B from the same origin at angle θ; a dashed line drops from the tip of B to A, and the length of A up to that point is labelled B cos θ. (b) A along the base and a longer B at angle θ; a dashed line from the tip of A meets B at a right angle, and the length of B up to that point is labelled A cos θ.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.2: (a) Projection of B on A, B cos θ; (b) projection of A on B, A cos θ (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.2).

blocks.text: For physical interpretation of dot product of two vectors A⃗ and B⃗, these are first brought to a common origin (Fig.2.2 a) then,

blocks.text_alt: A⃗.B⃗ = A (projection of B⃗ on A⃗)

blocks.latex: \text{or}\quad \vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = A\,(\text{magnitude of component of } \vec{B} \text{ in the direction of } \vec{A}),\ \text{Fig. 2.2(b)}
blocks.text_alt: or A⃗.B⃗ = A (magnitude of component of B⃗ in the direction of A⃗), Fig. 2.2(b)
= A (B cos θ) = AB cos θ
Similarly, B⃗.A⃗ = B (A cos θ) = BA cos θ

blocks.text: We come across this type of product when we consider the work done by a force F⃗ whose point of application moves a distance d in a direction making an angle θ with the line of action of F⃗, as shown in Fig. 2.3.

blocks.alt: A wooden block with a force F pulling from its corner at angle theta above the horizontal. The displacement d points along the horizontal; a dashed line drops from the tip of F to it, and F cos theta marks the part of F along d.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.3: Work done by a force F at angle θ to the displacement d (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.3).

blocks.latex: \text{Work done} = (\text{Effective component of force in the direction of motion}) \times \text{Distance moved}
blocks.text_alt: Work done = (Effective component of force in the direction of motion) × Distance moved
= (F cos θ) d = Fd cos θ
F⃗.d⃗ = Fd cos θ = Work done
